= JMAP AI Tools

This extension lets an AI assistant act on the user's mailbox. Twake Mail exposes a set of tools in the
OpenAI function-calling format: the assistant gives them to the LLM, and when the LLM picks one, the assistant
asks Twake Mail to run it for the user.

Twake Mail never calls the LLM here: the assistant owns the conversation, Twake Mail only describes and runs
the tools.

== Authentication and eligibility

Both endpoints use the JMAP authentication of the server (the strategies of `authentication.strategy.rfc8621`
in `jmap.properties`: Basic, JWT, OIDC...). Tools always run as the authenticated user, on their own mailboxes.

The user must also be eligible for AI features (the `ApplyWhenFilter` of the AI module, for example the SaaS
paying users). Otherwise both endpoints answer `401` with the detail `User is not eligible for AI tools`.

== List the tools

----
GET /ai/v1/tools
----

Returns every tool, sorted by name, in the OpenAI function-calling format, so the assistant can pass the list
to the LLM as is:

----
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "create_draft",
        "description": "Create an email draft in the user's **Drafts** folder. ...",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": { ... },
          "required": ["body"]
        }
      }
    },
    ...
  ]
}
----

== Run a tool

----
POST /ai/v1/tools
----

The body is the tool call returned by the LLM, as is. `arguments` can be a JSON object, or a string containing
a JSON object (as OpenAI sends it):

----
{
  "id": "call_123",
  "type": "function",
  "function": {
    "name": "search_emails",
    "arguments": "{\"unread\": true, \"after\": \"2026-10-13\"}"
  }
}
----

The answer is a `tool` message the assistant appends to the conversation. `content` is the result of the tool,
serialized as a JSON string:

----
{
  "role": "tool",
  "tool_call_id": "call_123",
  "content": "{\"emails\":[{\"id\":\"...\",\"from\":\"...\",\"subject\":\"...\",...}]}"
}
----

Numbers and booleans are also accepted as strings (`"limit": "5"`, `"unread": "true"`), as some assistants only
send strings.

=== Errors

Errors are JSON problem details (`status`, `detail`):

[cols="1,3"]
|===
| Status | When

| `400`
| The body is not JSON, `id` or `function.name` is missing, `function.arguments` is not a JSON object, or an
argument is invalid (for example `'limit' must be an integer`, `Missing 'body'`, `Invalid email id: ...`).

| `401`
| The user is not authenticated, or not eligible for AI tools.

| `404`
| Unknown tool (`Unknown tool: ...`), email not found or not readable by the user (`Email ... not found`),
mailbox not found or not readable by the user (`Mailbox not found`).

| `500`
| Unexpected error.
|===

== Tools

=== list_emails

Lists the emails of a mailbox, most recent first, as the user sees them. It is cheaper than `search_emails`,
and the LLM is told to try it first.

[cols="1,1,3"]
|===
| Argument | Type | Description

| `mailboxId` | string | Mailbox to list. The Inbox by default.
| `page` | integer | Page to return, from 1 (default) to 50.
| `limit` | integer | Emails per page: 10 by default, at most 20.
|===

Result:

----
{
  "mailboxId": "...",
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 10,
  "emails": [
    { "id": "...", "from": "Alice <alice@domain.tld>", "subject": "...", "receivedAt": "2026-10-14T09:00:00Z",
      "unread": true, "preview": "..." }
  ]
}
----

A user without an Inbox gets an empty list (`"mailboxId": null`). The preview is the one James computes for JMAP.

When `view.email.query.enabled` is `true` in `jmap.properties`, the emails are read from the email query view,
as JMAP `Email/query` does for a mailbox sorted by `receivedAt`. Otherwise they are read from the search index.

=== search_emails

Searches the emails of the user, most recent first. All filters are optional and combined with AND.

[cols="1,1,3"]
|===
| Argument | Type | Description

| `from` | string | Sender address or name.
| `to` | string | Recipient address or name.
| `text` | string | Text in the addresses, the subject, the body or the attachments (as the JMAP `text` filter).
| `after` | string | Only emails received after this date (ISO 8601: `2026-10-14` or `2026-10-14T10:00:00Z`).
| `before` | string | Only emails received before this date (ISO 8601).
| `inMailboxes` | array of strings | Only emails in one of these mailboxes. All the mailboxes by default.
| `unread` | boolean | Only unread (`true`) or read (`false`) emails.
| `limit` | integer | Maximum number of emails: 10 by default, at most 20.
|===

Result: `{ "emails": [ ... ] }`, each email as in `list_emails`.

=== get_email_details

Reads one email, for example to summarize it or to reply to it.

[cols="1,1,3"]
|===
| Argument | Type | Description

| `id` | string | *Required.* Id of the email, as returned by `list_emails` or `search_emails`.
|===

Result:

----
{
  "id": "...",
  "from": ["Alice <alice@domain.tld>"],
  "to": ["paying@domain.tld"],
  "cc": [],
  "subject": "...",
  "receivedAt": "2026-10-14T08:30:00Z",
  "mailboxIds": ["..."],
  "unread": true,
  "attachments": ["report.pdf"],
  "body": "...",
  "truncated": false
}
----

The body is the text of the email (the text extracted from the HTML for an HTML only email), cut after 5000
characters (`truncated` is then `true`).

=== create_draft

Creates a draft in the user's `Drafts` mailbox (created if missing). The draft is never sent: the assistant can
open it in a composer so that the user reviews it and sends it.

[cols="1,1,3"]
|===
| Argument | Type | Description

| `to` | array of strings | Recipient addresses.
| `cc` | array of strings | CC addresses.
| `subject` | string | Subject. For a reply without subject, `Re: ` and the subject of the original email.
| `body` | string | *Required.* Body, in Markdown.
| `inReplyTo` | string | Id of the email this draft replies to: sets `In-Reply-To` and `References`, so the reply stays in the thread.
|===

Result: `{ "id": "...", "mailboxId": "...", "subject": "..." }`, `id` being the id of the draft.

The draft is flagged as a draft and as seen (`$draft` and `$seen` in JMAP). Its body is a `multipart/alternative`: the Markdown as `text/plain`,
and its rendering as `text/html`. Raw HTML written in the body is escaped, and `javascript:` links are dropped.
